__baseline_prompt__.text: Create a natural sports photograph of the reference-guided sportsperson during a sporting practice moment. Use the supplied photograph as the face and hair appearance reference. Preserve the reference's visible facial structure and short dark bob with fine forehead strands. The swimmer is poised on a swimming starting block at an indoor lane pool, gathering into a track-start position just before a practice launch. The held breath before movement is the photograph's center: a quiet, concentrated face above a compact arrangement of loaded limbs, with the empty lane opening ahead. The swimmer wears a plain deep-navy one-piece training swimsuit. Damp bobbed hair is tucked behind the ears, retaining its short rounded silhouette and fine front strands. The head lifts slightly along the lane so the face reads in three-quarter view; the mouth is gently parted and the gaze settles on the water ahead. The poised body line, close-fitting sport fabric and delicate wet highlights give the person a subtle, unforced appeal within the athletic situation. Both hands belong to the swimmer and grip the two front corners of the block, fingers curling over its front lip outside the knees. The forward forefoot bears on the flat textured platform with the toes curled over the leading edge between the hands. The rear forefoot presses into the raised rear wedge, its heel lifted. The flexed knees are separated enough to reveal the rear foot's wedge contact; each leg traces continuously from hip through knee to its own foot. The hips sit above the shoulders, with the torso folded forward and the arms descending beside the knees. These are simultaneous supports in a still loaded start, with the swimmer's entire body remaining above the block. Photograph from a slightly elevated front-side three-quarter position looking across the block toward the lane. A landscape frame includes the entire swimmer, both hands, both feet, the full block and its base, with a margin of deck and water around them. Make the front-lip hand contacts, forward-toe platform contact and rear-foot wedge contact individually readable in the same exposure. The clear aqua lane and receding lane ropes carry the eye forward. Soft high windows give clean skin tones, small water beads and gentle reflections on the wet deck, while the swimmer and block remain the sharp visual center.
